forcedChoices.choice: «toma de conciencia de su divinidad» instead of the earlier glossary form «autorrealización»
forcedChoices.reason: Here self-realization means that Jesus became aware of his own divinity; Spanish «autorrealización» reads as self-fulfillment, a sense the authors did not intend.
The English form «seraphim» is plural; the context does not say one or two, so the plural form of the English is kept.

forcedChoices.choice: «los dos de Nazaret» for «the Nazareth couple»
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish «pareja» suggests a romantic couple, and «nazarenos» has a religious sense.
Spanish forces a choice between lifestyle and spiritual way; «camino» keeps both readings best.
This Saul is Paul of Tarsus; «Saúl» in the glossary is the king.

forcedChoices.choice: «tú» from the Roman magistrate to Jesus
forcedChoices.reason: A magistrate speaks down to a provincial; nothing shows respect from him to Jesus.
The English does not give the gender of Ruth's playmates; the masculine plural is the generic form.
«con sus padres» can be read as his parents only.
The glossary form «pacto» is for covenant; «actual» here is the plain adjective, not the technical term «en acto».
